findings.description: The statistics dict is now shared by every call to the decorated function and is cleared on each new call, so concurrent calls from different threads overwrite each other's in-flight statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same decorated function at once. Mechanism: each call runs stats.clear() on the single dict that was previously a per-call copy, so one thread's begin() wipes or rewrites the counters another thread is still reading. Impact: a retry callback or code reading wrapped.statistics during a call can observe attempt_number, start_time or idle_for values belonging to a different call.

findings.description: The async wrapper clears and reuses one shared statistics dict across all invocations, so concurrent awaits of the same decorated coroutine corrupt each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two tasks await the same decorated async function concurrently, e.g. via asyncio.gather. Mechanism: stats.clear() on the shared dict resets state that the other in-flight call is still updating, and the dict is mutated across interleaved awaits. Impact: statistics seen by one call's callbacks or by the caller reflect the other call's attempts and timings.
